obligations.note: The change sets payments PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES and payments.privileged_idle_minutes to 16, which breaks the catalog bound of <= 15. No valid exception covers this deviation.

The cited exception EXC-0189 is scoped to component mortgage.session (Mortgage privileged sessions), not payments.session. The only payments.session exception, EXC-0141, expired on 2026-09-05, before the 2026-10-05 review time. No in-scope, unexpired exception exists.
Ticket CHG-24519 was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-02, before the change opened. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both touched paths.
The code_review approval is from Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver who is not the author Jonah Weiss under any of his listed addresses.
Both approvals name the head commit 31160f7, which is the only commit on the change.

CI run.json shows the full payments suite run on head 31160f7: 172 tests, 0 failures or skips. That includes the registered SES-1 control test. The JUnit timestamp and hostname look inconsistent with the CI run, but this does not change the outcome. A pass also does not cure the bound violation.
No security_sensitive component is touched: payments.policy and payments.controls-data are both marked non-sensitive. No security review is required.
controls/payments/policy-params.json is a protected path. Rachel Stein (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so no PIR is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers the changed symbol (PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES) or the session code, so no ledger evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1845 raises the payments privileged idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes, directly violating SES-1's bound of at most 15 minutes. The change relies on exception EXC-0189, but that exception is scoped to mortgage.session, not payments.session. The payments exception EXC-0141 expired before review. Ticket, independent code review, control-owner approval and CI are otherwise in order, but process approvals cannot cure an unexcepted violation of a product obligation. The change is rejected.
